about.title: Duarte Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Duarte residents rely on countless everyday products — from vehicle parts driven along I-210 and Huntington Drive to household appliances and tools used at home or on the job. When one of those products is defective, the resulting injury can be severe and unexpected. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim, meaning you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This can apply to defects in design, manufacturing, or inadequate warnings. We're here to help evaluate your case. Preserving the product itself, along with packaging and any related paperwork, can be an important early step. Reaching out for a free case review costs nothing and creates no obligation.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Ease Your Burden
items.desc: California generally doesn't require proof the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may broaden your options for pursuing a claim.

items.title: Design, Manufacturing, and Warning Defects All Count
items.desc: Whether the flaw was in how a product was designed, built, or labeled, we can help evaluate which theory fits your situation.

items.question: I no longer have the product that hurt me — can I still have a case?
items.answer: It's harder without the physical product, but not necessarily impossible. Photos, packaging, receipts, or the retailer's records can sometimes help. We can review what evidence you do have and advise you on next steps.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: No. Under California's strict liability framework, you generally don't need to show the manufacturer was careless or aware of the flaw. You typically just need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury.

items.question: Does it matter that the product was bought outside Duarte?
items.answer: Not usually. What matters more is where the injury happened and where you live, since that often determines which courts and laws apply. We can sort out these details for your specific situation.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. Our initial case review is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
